text: TCG Yavuz (F 240) is the lead ship of the Yavuz-class frigate in the Turkish Navy. These frigates were designed in Germany as part of the MEKO family, specifically the MEKO 200 design, and were ordered by the Turkish government in April 1983 for four vessels. Two ships were constructed in Germany and two in Turkey with German support. The Yavuz-class frigates share a similar design with the larger Barbaros-class frigates, which are enhanced versions of the Yavuz-class. The Turkish Navy is currently conducting a limited modernization program to upgrade the Yavuz-class frigates with locally produced electronic countermeasures (ECM), electronic counter-countermeasures (ECCM), active decoys, low-frequency radar warning receivers (LWRs), infrared search and track (IRST) systems, and associated user interface systems. TCG Yavuz was launched on 30 May 1985 by Blohm+Voss in Hamburg and officially commissioned on 11 October 1987. On 11 September 2020, she escorted TCG İskenderun in the Mediterranean during its journey to the Port of Marmaris. Media related to TCG Yavuz (F-240) is available at Wikimedia Commons.
